info.name: Balance Service
info.description:
Functional scenarios for the Concurrent Balance Service REST API. Run the folders in order: later requests assert balances produced by earlier ones. Every run uses a fresh id prefix (`run`), so it can be repeated against the same server.

Postman sends requests one at a time, so concurrency is not covered here; it is covered by the Java contract suite (`BalanceServiceContractTest`).

item.name: 1. Setup
item.description: Open two accounts; opening the same id again is rejected.

exec: pm.test("Location header points at the balance", () => pm.response.to.have.header("Location"));
// A fresh prefix for every run, so the collection can be rerun without resetting data.
pm.test("Location header points at the balance", () => pm.response.to.have.header("Location"));

item.name: 2. Balance
item.description: Read a balance; an unknown account is 404.

item.name: 3. Credit and debit
item.description: The brief's examples; an overdraft fails and changes nothing.

item.name: 4. Transfer
item.description: A transfer moves the exact amount; a failed one changes neither account.

item.name: 5. Idempotency
item.description: Replaying a transactionId succeeds but applies once; reusing it for a different request is 409.

item.name: Transfer 50 from A to B with TX-i2 (1st) → 204
Transfer 50 from A to B with TX-i2 (2nd) → 204
6. Validation
item.description: Invalid input is rejected before anything changes.

item.name: Transfer from A to an unknown account → 404
7. Retry after failure
item.description: A failed operation does not use up its transactionId.

item.name: 8. Reports
item.description: The live report endpoints behind /reports/accounts.html and /reports/transactions.html. Other runs' data may be present too, so assertions filter to this run's ids.

exec: pm.test("this run: A is 550 and B is 850", () => pm.expect(mine).to.eql({ A: 550, B: 850 }));

item.name: 9. Delete account
item.description: Deleting discards the balance; the account then behaves as if it never existed, and its id can never be used again.

exec: pm.test("Location header points at the balance", () => pm.response.to.have.header("Location"));

item.name: Accounts report no longer lists C

exec: pm.test("this run lists A and B only", () => pm.expect(mine).to.eql(["A", "B"]));
